description:
Save and load for Noodloft components. Source-generated JSON, pluggable stores, per-entry
            versioning, and a merging save that does not wipe the state of scenes that are not loaded.
            Configuration is never written to disk, so rebalancing takes effect on existing saves.
releaseNotes:
Fixes from a review of `v0.0.1-alpha4`. Four of these could lose or corrupt a player's save.

### Fixed

- **A save could be silently downgraded and corrupted.** `SaveSession.Save` merged whatever it found
  in the slot without looking at its schema version, then stamped the result with this build's. A slot
  written by a newer build was read with the parts this build happened to recognise, rewritten as the
  older format, and the rest of it lost — irreversibly. Loading already refused a newer format;
  saving, the more destructive of the two, did not. It now refuses a newer schema unless `Overwrite`
  is explicit, and migrates an older one before carrying its entries forward.
- **A subsequent save erased the slot's metadata.** `options.Metadata` was written unconditionally, so
  the first ordinary autosave after a metadata-bearing one replaced the area name and playtime a load
  menu reads with nothing — despite the format documenting metadata as round-tripped untouched. A save
  that supplies no metadata now carries forward what is already there. Pass an empty dictionary, or
  `Overwrite`, to clear it deliberately.
- **`GodotUserSaveStore` deleted the previous save before renaming the new one into place**, leaving a
  window in which the slot did not exist at all — the exact window a write-then-rename removes, and
  the opposite of what the comment above it claimed. The previous file is now moved aside and only
  removed once the new one has landed; a failed rename puts it back. Renaming straight over the old
  file would be one step instead of three, but only POSIX guarantees that replaces atomically, so the
  short version is safe on the developer's machine and not on half the players'.
- **NaN could reach a health pool and poison it permanently.** `Math.Clamp` passes NaN straight through
  — every comparison against it is false — and NaN survives all later arithmetic, so a single one left
  a pool that could never be healed or damaged again. The evaluator now declines it and returns the
  value unchanged, exactly as it already did for division by zero.
- **Health reported `Applied` for operations that changed nothing.** Healing a full pool, adding zero
  and every operation the evaluator declined all raised `OnModelSet`, and Godot's `HealthChanged`
  behind it, for a pool that had not moved — against the contract the rest of the library is built on.
  They now report `Unchanged`.
- **Disposing an older node could unregister a newer one.** Registration deliberately lets the later of
  two claimants on a save id win, but unregistration removed by id alone. Two scenes overlap during a
  transition — the incoming one is ready before the outgoing one is freed — so the outgoing node took
  the live registration with it and the new scene was silently never saved. `SaveSession.Unregister`
  gained an overload that removes a participant only if it is still the registered one, and the nodes
  use it.
- **The movement input nodes applied two dead zones.** They read `GetActionStrength`, which has already
  applied the action's own dead zone from Project Settings, and the component then applied its
  circular one on top — so a stick had to clear a square threshold and then a round one, and the usable
  range began well past where either was configured. They now read `GetActionRawStrength`.
- **`OrbitCamera3D` only warned about needing physics processing, and did not enforce it.** Avoid
  Geometry casts a ray, which is only safe during a physics frame; a value set from code or a warning
  read and ignored left it running from `_Process`. The node now selects physics processing itself
  whenever Avoid Geometry is on, and keeps the warning for the case somebody can see it.
- **`TickMode.Manual` on the camera nodes had no way to tick them.** Added `ManualTick(float)`,
  matching `PersistentComponentNode`.

### Changed

- **The packages multi-target net8.0 as well as net10.0.** net8.0 is what Godot 4.4 gives a C# project
  by default, so a net10.0-only package failed to install with NU1201 in the very engine version the
  addon names as its floor. The test projects target both, so the net8.0 asset is executed rather than
  merely compiled, and CI installs both runtimes; running the whole suite locally now needs the .NET 8
  runtime alongside the SDK.

### Added

- 15 regression tests covering every fix above, including a schema-5 slot surviving a save from a
  schema-2 build, metadata outliving a later save, an overlapping registration not being unregistered
  by the node on its way out, and a health pool still working after a NaN was refused.
